title: GENTLE-01 — Low-force gripper
evidence:
The brief contains a candidate architecture, illustrative force calculations and sensitivity plots, fault-handling requirements, and a proposed validation program. It states that no hardware was built or tested. No measured delicate-object performance, damage-free guarantee, affordability, or superiority is established.

Candidate architecture: independently driven jaws, per-jaw output limiting, compliant instrumented fingertips, normal-load sensing, and optical slip cues. Optical sensing may request only bounded force changes; it is not an independent certified force limit. Pad identity and calibration must remain linked after replacement.

All forces in the worked examples are per finger. For an illustrative 100 g object, friction lower bound 0.40 gives a required normal force of 1.933 N and a command interval of 2.033–2.650 N. At friction 0.25, the required force rises to 3.093 N and the command interval is empty: 3.193–2.650 N, so the model refuses the grasp.

These numbers use assumed acceleration, load margin, force uncertainty, overshoot, and damage limit. They are not measured gripper specifications. The model does not qualify torsional slip, off-center loads, impacts, adhesion, changing contact area, or evolving material damage. Limiting resultant normal force does not establish a local pressure limit.

Proposed first bench targets are 20–60 mm object width, 20–100 g mass, and at most 10 mm clearance above a padded catch surface. These are unqualified development targets. Full end-effector mass, inertia, center of mass, cabling, and allowed robot stop profiles still require integration assessment.

The brief's reliability illustration states that zero failures in 100 independent, identically distributed trials gives a one-sided 95% upper failure-probability bound of approximately 2.951%. Repeated grasps on one specimen do not establish independence or broad reliability. No such prototype trial result is claimed.

Saved software test record: 15 tests passed. This website update reviewed the committed record; it did not rerun the suite.

Committed simulation plan: seed 20261019; 20,000 families; 100 trials per family; alpha 0.01; mean on-background 0.2; off/on exposure ratio 10; injected signal mean 6.

Null family false-alert rates: uncorrected known background 10.605%; Bonferroni known background 0.590%; Bonferroni with naive estimated background 91.695%; Bonferroni exact on/off 0.105% (95% Clopper–Pearson interval 0.0650%–0.1605%). These are separate procedures under the committed simulation settings, not detector performance ratings.

Injected-window power: 65.625% (95% interval 64.962%–66.283%). Unflagged rate-shift stress: 32.445% alert rate. Unflagged overdispersion stress: 50.925%. These stress results expose failures when model assumptions are violated.

Assumptions: fixed windows and cuts; stationary equal on/off rates; independent on/off Poisson counts; full exposure; trusted quality metadata. Bonferroni requires valid marginal p-values, not independence between test windows.

Limits: per-family false-alert probability, not yearly false-alarm rate or astrophysical discovery significance. No real observations, full particle/light transport, or spatial likelihood. No blind human custody of the synthetic data. Hardware remains unvalidated.

title: GRASP-01 — Grasp-recovery simulation benchmark
evidence:
The saved report embeds a seeded simulation manifest, aggregate outcomes, and selected recorded trajectories. There are 800 scenario instances per policy, or 2,400 policy episodes in total. Families: nominal, friction step, heavy payload, sensor dropout, force bias, slow actuator, fragility mismatch, and combined faults.

Saved aggregate results:
fixed: 550/800 complete; 10 controlled set-downs; 235 drops; 0 grip-damage events; 240 impact-damage events; 240 failures.
reactive: 518/800 complete; 10 controlled set-downs; 126 drops; 164 grip-damage events; 126 impact-damage events; 272 failures.
guarded: 385/800 complete; 231 controlled set-downs; 100 drops; 98 grip-damage events; 105 impact-damage events; 184 failures.

Failure flags can overlap; drops, grip damage, and impact damage must not be summed as independent outcomes. Controlled set-down is not task completion.

Guarded recovery completed 48.125% of episodes, versus 68.750% fixed and 64.750% reactive. Its drop rate was 12.500%, versus 29.375% fixed and 15.750% reactive. Its grip-damage rate was 12.250%, versus 0% fixed and 20.500% reactive. Guarded control therefore did not dominate both baselines on all metrics.

The strict undamaged slip-settling diagnostic recorded zero successful recoveries for all three policies. Slipped episodes were 268 fixed, 261 reactive, and 137 guarded; all remained failed or censored under that diagnostic. Set-down counts must not be relabeled as successful slip recovery.

Physics checks run at a modeled 500 Hz; control packets and replay frames are 50 Hz. The report gives pointwise Wilson intervals and 2,000 stratified paired bootstrap resamples for differences, without multiplicity correction. These describe this artificial suite, not real factory prevalence or hardware reliability. This website update inspected saved data and arithmetic; it did not rerun the Python benchmark.

title: Retinal Flood Map — Retinal mapping research
Roman Concrete — Finite-reserve self-healing model
evidence:
The saved audit reports execution of two supplied demos unchanged. Neither implements a displacement/equilibrium solve, pressure-driven capillary flow or finite lime-calcium supply.

Capacity check under the starter's own one-to-one reaction law: maximum porosity drop = volume per mole × available reaction capacity. At 3 × 10⁻⁵ m³/mol and 250 mol/m³, the limit is 0.0075; a crack starting at porosity 0.80 cannot fall below 0.7925 through that law alone. The demo instead uses a volume per mole 500 times larger, changing attainable sealing rather than merely accelerating time.

A uniform interior-cell check in the first script creates 0.000599976 mol/m³ calcium in one two-second step, a 0.240% inventory error. Its open-crack fraction remains 0.089375 from step 50 through step 399, so that metric does not demonstrate closure.

A periodic transport test also finds a nonzero net numerical divergence. The audit recommends conservative shared-face fluxes and direct updates of stored calcium.

These are saved code-level diagnostics, not experiments. No material-calibrated healing time, recovered structural strength, repaired multiphysics solver or 2,000-year prediction is established.
contributors:
Independent numerical audit archived with Mr. Peloquin's research collection. Authorship of the two original scripts is not identified in the supplied files and remains unresolved.

Scientific background: Linda M. Seymour and coauthors (2023), hot-mixing and lime-clast mechanisms; Marie D. Jackson and coauthors (2017), Roman marine-concrete mineral cements. title: Temporal Acoustics
evidence:
2D scalar finite-difference wave propagation with a circular pressure-release void surrogate, five synthetic source positions, thirteen receivers along one depth, a known 900 Hz pulse, effective-speed calibration and diffraction-style migration. This is not coupled elastic P/S-wave tomography.

Eight randomized synthetic rock worlds, with two independent noisy acquisitions per class, produced 16 cavity-present and 16 cavity-absent cases. A held-out-world threshold trained on smoother no-cavity controls gave 100% sensitivity and 12.5% false-positive rate for the calibrated global-peak score in this small simulated sample. This is not field performance, and the peak is not a calibrated probability.

Eight additional negative controls with sharp 35%-slower solid inclusions were deliberately outside the smooth-null calibration distribution. The calibrated interior-peak rule falsely flagged five of eight inclusions as cavities. Median location error for planted cavities across the varied worlds remained approximately 1.00 m. An 11%-faster deep synthetic lens and uniform rock produced the same short-offset calibrated speed (~2542 m/s), showing the inability of this direct-arrival geometry to constrain deep rock properties.

Ten unit tests passed; reproducible source, exact inputs, metrics, and plotted controls are linked. No actual measurements of Malta, pyramids, cart ruts, caves or historical buildings were used.

title: Temporal Reflection Chamber
evidence:
Published temporal-reflection experiments provide precedent for engineered transmission lines; they do not validate this proposed apparatus or a room-wide temporal interface. The archive reports numerical/algebraic checks by Wolfram Language and Python, not hardware simulation or experimental verification.

Ideal geometry calculations for an 8-foot air-filled conducting cube give a lowest resonance of 86.936220 MHz and an air-crossing time of 8.133627 ns. Real construction changes losses and modes; air-crossing time is not a trigger-skew budget.

In an ideal uniform nondispersive line with fixed inductance and capacitance multiplied by r, velocity, impedance and frequency magnitude scale as 1/sqrt(r). For r=4 the ideal backward-arrival relation is t_b=3t_s−2t_i at the same reference plane. These are conditional planning predictions; actual dispersion, switching, receiver and cable delays require calibration.

Proposed evidence combines reversed feature order, duration and frequency scaling, arrival-time sweeps, asymmetric waveform repeats and source-off/static/bypass/boundary-switch controls. None of those proposed gates is reported as passed. Ordinary echoes, mixing and switching artifacts remain competing explanations.

No stopped time, long-term broadcast retention, net energy gain or unusual conservation behavior is established.
